evidence.notes: The local runtime accepts AccessLevel and returns the same no-delivery SaveResult as EventBus.publish.
The callback overload reuses local EventBus.publish callback handling and ignores AccessLevel.
The list overload returns ordered local SaveResult values and ignores AccessLevel.
The list callback overload returns ordered local SaveResult values and ignores AccessLevel.

source.content: Database.SaveResult one = EventBus.publishWithAccessLevel(new Account(Name = 'User'), AccessLevel.USER_MODE); System.assert(one.isSuccess()); Database.SaveResult two = EventBus.publishWithAccessLevel(new Account(Name = 'Callback'), null, AccessLevel.USER_MODE); System.assert(two.isSuccess()); List<Database.SaveResult> three = EventBus.publishWithAccessLevel(new List<Account>{new Account(Name = 'List')}, AccessLevel.SYSTEM_MODE); System.assertEquals(1, three.size()); System.assert(three[0].isSuccess()); List<Database.SaveResult> four = EventBus.publishWithAccessLevel(new List<Account>{new Account(Name = 'ListCallback')}, null, AccessLevel.SYSTEM_MODE); System.assertEquals(1, four.size()); System.assert(four[0].isSuccess());
